mainTopic: Punishment and decrees for one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman, the limits of קנאין פוגעין בו, and the story of זמרי and פנחס
overview: The גמרא asks what happens to a man who had relations with a non-Jewish woman if the קנאין did not strike him. רב had forgotten his tradition, but a dream given to רב כהנא brings a פסוק in מלאכי that reminds him. The next פסוק answers the question: ה׳ cuts off his line, so a תלמיד חכם will have no scholarly descendants and a כהן will have no son who serves. רבי חייא בר אבויה adds that such a man is like one who marries into עבודה זרה, and he tells the story of יהויקים's skull, which was thrown out and later burned. רב דימי and רבין report a decree of the חשמונאים that makes this man liable on several counts. They argue whether a non-Jewish woman counts as an אשת איש or a זונה. The גמרא then limits the zealot's right: בית דין gives no permission to one who asks, a zealot may act only during the act, and the sinner may defend himself. Finally the גמרא tells the story of זמרי and כזבי, why פנחס acted, and how he carried the spear, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What if the zealots did not strike him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is for a man with a non-Jewish woman if the קנאין never punished him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If zealots did not strike him, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the man the משנה said zealots may strike: what happens if no zealot actually did? This sets up everything that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said קנאין פוגעין בו, meaning zealots may strike him on the spot. That is not a court punishment, so if no zealot acted, it is unclear whether he faces any punishment at all. The question asks what his punishment is in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Zealots, people who act on the spot out of zeal for ה׳
What is it? What is the law?

phrases.english: If zealots did not strike him, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "Him" is the man from the משנה who had relations with a non-Jewish woman.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What punishment, if any, applies to one who had relations with a non-Jewish woman when the קנאין did not strike him.

steps.title: רב forgets, and רב כהנא has a dream
steps.stepSummary: רב forgot the answer he had received. A פסוק from מלאכי was read to רב כהנא in a dream, and he told רב about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב forgot his tradition. In a dream, they read to רב כהנא the פסוק: "Judah has dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and Jerusalem, for Judah has profaned the sacred of ה׳ which He loves, and has been intimate with the daughter of a strange god." He came and told רב: this is what they read to me.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story. רב cannot remember the answer, but a dream gives רב כהנא a פסוק, and he brings it to רב. It sets up רב remembering in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not reached by argument. It comes from a tradition רב had lost, and the dream supplies the פסוק that will jog his memory. The last phrase of the פסוק, "daughter of a strange god," is the part that connects to our case.

keyTerms.meaning: His learning, the tradition he received from his teachers
They read to him, they caused him to read

phrases.english: Rav forgot his tradition.
They read to Rav Kahana in his dream:
"Judah has dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חִלֵּל יְהוּדָה קֹדֶשׁ ה׳ אֲשֶׁר אָהֵב
phrases.english: for Judah has profaned the sacred of ה׳, which He loves,
and has been intimate with the daughter of a strange god."
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:11

phrases.english: He came and said to him: This is what they read to me.
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is telling רב about his dream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב could not answer right away and how the answer's source came to him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The source for the answer is the פסוק in מלאכי 2:11, revealed in a dream.

steps.title: רב remembers: idol worship and forbidden male relations
steps.stepSummary: רב remembers his tradition and explains the first two parts of the פסוק: "dealt treacherously" is עבודה זרה, and "abomination" is משכב זכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב remembered his tradition. "Judah has dealt treacherously" means עבודה זרה, as it says: "So you have dealt treacherously with Me, house of Israel, says ה׳." "An abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem" means משכב זכור, as it says: "Do not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination."
steps.whatsHappening: The dream works, and רב remembers. He starts explaining the פסוק phrase by phrase, proving each meaning from another פסוק that uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is matched to a sin through a shared word. "בגד" (treachery) is used in ירמיהו for Israel betraying ה׳, which means idol worship. "תועבה" (abomination) is the word the Torah uses for משכב זכור.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says, introducing a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: Rav remembered his tradition.
"Judah has dealt treacherously": this is idol worship,
and so it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֵּן בְּגַדְתֶּם בִּי בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל נְאֻם ה׳״.
phrases.english: "So you have dealt treacherously with Me, house of Israel, says ה׳."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:20

phrases.english: "And an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem":
this is male-male relations,
and so it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאֶת זָכָר לֹא תִשְׁכַּב מִשְׁכְּבֵי אִשָּׁה תּוֹעֵבָה הִיא״.
phrases.english: "Do not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב, now reminded, begins explaining the פסוק from the dream.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In מלאכי 2:11, "בגדה" refers to עבודה זרה and "תועבה" refers to משכב זכור.

steps.title: The prostitute, and one with a non-Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: רב explains the last two parts of the פסוק: "profaned the sacred" is a זונה, and "daughter of a strange god" is הבא על הגויה, which is our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: "For Judah has profaned the sacred of ה׳" means a זונה, as it says: "There shall be no קדשה among the daughters of Israel." "And has been intimate with the daughter of a strange god" means one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes explaining the פסוק. Its last phrase turns out to be about our exact case, the man with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "קודש" is linked to "קדשה" (a prostitute) because they share the same root. Most importantly, "daughter of a strange god" is our case, so this פסוק, and the one right after it, speaks directly to our question.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who acts promiscuously, a prostitute
One who has relations with a non-Jewish woman

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the פסוק to our case, so the punishment in the next פסוק applies to him.

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי חִלֵּל יְהוּדָה קֹדֶשׁ ה׳״ – זוֹ זוֹנָה,
phrases.english: "For Judah has profaned the sacred of ה׳": this is a prostitute,
and so it says:
"There shall be no prostitute among the daughters of Israel."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:18. "קדשה" comes from the same root as "קודש" in our פסוק, and that's the link.

phrases.aramaic: ״וּבָעַל בַּת אֵל נֵכָר״ – זֶה הַבָּא עַל הַגּוֹיָה.
phrases.english: "And has been intimate with the daughter of a strange god": this is one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי חִלֵּל יְהוּדָה קֹדֶשׁ ה׳ זוֹ זוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's phrase-by-phrase explanation and reaches our case.
steps.raayaObject: That מלאכי 2:11 speaks about one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase "ובעל בת אל נכר" in מלאכי 2:11.

steps.title: The answer: his line is cut off
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק says ה׳ will cut off this man. A תלמיד חכם will have no scholarly descendants, and a כהן will have no son who brings offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written after it: "May ה׳ cut off the man who does this, one who calls and one who answers, from the tents of Jacob, and one who brings an offering to ה׳ of hosts." If he is a תלמיד חכם, he will have no one who calls among the Sages or answers among the students. If he is a כהן, he will have no son who brings an offering to ה׳ of hosts.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the actual answer to the question from step 1. If the zealots did not strike him, ה׳ punishes him by cutting off his descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק (מלאכי 2:12) describes the punishment for the sins just listed, including ours. The גמרא reads "one who calls and one who answers" as scholarly descendants, and "one who brings an offering" as a כהן son. So the punishment fits who he is.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written after it
One who calls (raises points) and one who answers
One who brings an offering (a כהן's job)

steps.whatToRemember: If the קנאין did not strike a man who had relations with a non-Jewish woman, ה׳ cuts off his line. A scholar loses scholarly descendants, and a כהן loses sons who serve in the מקדש.

phrases.english: And it is written after it:
"May ה׳ cut off the man who does this,
one who calls and one who answers, from the tents of Jacob,
and one who brings an offering to ה׳ of hosts."
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:12

phrases.english: If he is a Torah scholar,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ עֵר בַּחֲכָמִים וְעוֹנֶה בַּתַּלְמִידִים.
phrases.english: he will have no one who calls among the Sages or answers among the students.
phrases.notes: "He will have" means among his descendants: no child of his will be a scholar.

phrases.english: If he is a kohen,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בֵּן מַגִּישׁ מִנְחָה לַה׳ צְבָאוֹת.
phrases.english: he will have no son who brings an offering to ה׳ of hosts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the פסוק is shown to be about our case, the next פסוק gives its punishment.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If the קנאין did not strike him, ה׳ cuts off his descendants: no scholarly offspring for a תלמיד חכם, and no son serving in the מקדש for a כהן.

steps.title: Like marrying into idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבויה teaches that one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman is like one who marries into עבודה זרה, since the פסוק calls her "daughter of a strange god."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבויה said: Anyone who has relations with a non-Jewish woman is as though he married into idol worship, as it is written: "and has been intimate with the daughter of a strange god." Does a strange god have a daughter? Rather, this is one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds a lesson from the same phrase in the פסוק. He shows how serious this sin is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol obviously has no daughter, so the phrase must mean a woman who belongs to an idol-worshipping people. Because the פסוק calls her the idol's "daughter," being with her is like becoming the idol's son-in-law.

keyTerms.meaning: Marries into, becomes related by marriage

steps.confusionAlert: "Does a strange god have a daughter?" is not a challenge to anyone. It is רבי חייא בר אבויה's own question, showing the words cannot be meant literally.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Avuya said:
Anyone who has relations with a non-Jewish woman,
it is as though he married into idol worship,
as it is written: "and has been intimate with the daughter of a strange god."

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי בַּת יֵשׁ לוֹ לְאֵל נֵכָר?
phrases.english: Does a strange god have a daughter?
Rather, this is one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same phrase רב explained to teach how severe the sin is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who has relations with a non-Jewish woman is as though he married into עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Words written on the skull of King יהויקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבויה teaches that the words 'This and yet another' were written on the skull of יהויקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבויה said: On the skull of יהויקים it was written, 'This and yet another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from רבי חייא בר אבויה, the same אמורא from the last step. It sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase means one punishment has already come, and another is still on the way. The story that follows will show how both parts came true for יהויקים.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked king of יהודה shortly before the חורבן
'This and yet another': one punishment plus one more

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Avuya said:
It was written on the skull of Yehoyakim
"This and yet another."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same אמורא as step 6. It is linked to that step by the speaker, not by the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The skull of יהויקים carried the words 'This and yet another,' a sign that more punishment awaited him.

steps.title: The skull keeps coming back up out of the ground
steps.stepSummary: The grandfather of רבי פרידא finds a skull at the gates of ירושלים with the words on it. Every time he buries it, it comes back up, so he realizes it belongs to יהויקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The grandfather of רבי פרידא found a skull lying at the gates of ירושלים, with 'This and yet another' written on it. He buried it, and it came back up. He buried it again, and it came back up again. He said: This is the skull of יהויקים, about whom it is written, 'With the burial of a donkey he shall be buried, dragged and thrown beyond the gates of ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: A story backs up the teaching from step 7. The skull will not stay buried, so the finder knows whose it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו said יהויקים would get a donkey's burial and be thrown outside the gates of ירושלים. A skull that keeps coming back up near those gates fits that פסוק exactly, so it must be his. This is the first punishment, the 'This.'

keyTerms.meaning: It came back up out of the ground
A donkey's burial, meaning no real burial at all

phrases.english: The grandfather of Rabbi Perida
phrases.notes: This seems to be רבי חייא בר אבויה himself, which is why the story comes right after his teaching.

phrases.english: found a certain skull
that was lying thrown at the gates of Jerusalem,
and written on it was "This and yet another."
He buried it, and it came back up;
he buried it, and it came back up again.
He said: This is the skull of Yehoyakim,
about whom it is written:
"With the burial of a donkey he shall be buried,
dragged and thrown beyond the gates of Jerusalem."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 22:19

steps.triggerLanguage: זְקֵינוֹ דְּרַבִּי פְּרִידָא אַשְׁכַּח הָהוּא גּוּלְגֻּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story behind the teaching in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 7 that the skull of יהויקים bore these words.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The real event at the gates of ירושלים, matched to ירמיהו 22:19.

steps.title: He honors the skull, but his wife burns it
steps.stepSummary: Because יהויקים was a king, the finder wraps the skull in silk and keeps it in a chest. His wife sees it, and the neighbors tell her it is his first wife's skull. In anger, she burns it in the oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: He is a king, and it is not proper to disgrace him. He took the skull, wrapped it in silk, and put it in a chest. His wife came and saw it. She went out and told her neighbors. They told her: This is the skull of his first wife, whom he has not forgotten. She heated the oven and burned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The man tries to treat the skull with honor, but his wife ends up burning it. This sets up the final line in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's plan was to give the king some dignity. Through a misunderstanding, the skull suffers something worse than being thrown outside: it is burned. That burning is the 'another' punishment.

phrases.english: He said: He is a king,
and it is not proper to disgrace him.
He took it and wrapped it in silk,
and placed it in a chest.
His wife came and saw it.
She went out and told her neighbors.
They said to her:
This is the skull of the first wife,
whom he has not forgotten.
She heated the oven and burned it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: מַלְכָּא הוּא, וְלָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְבַזּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. After the skull is identified, the man tries to honor it, and it gets burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The attempt to honor יהויקים led to his skull being burned, an extra disgrace.

steps.title: This is what 'This and yet another' meant
steps.stepSummary: When the man comes home and finds out what happened, he realizes the burning was the 'another' written on the skull.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came, he said: This is what was written on it, 'This and yet another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by explaining the words on the skull. Being thrown out was the first punishment, and being burned was the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the loop from step 7. 'This' is the donkey's burial outside the gates, and 'another' is the burning. Even the man's good intentions could not stop what was written.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what is written; this explains the words

steps.whatToRemember: יהויקים was punished twice: his remains were thrown outside ירושלים, and later his skull was burned. That is the meaning of 'This and yet another.'

phrases.english: When he came, he said:
This is what was written on it:
"This and yet another."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the burning from step 9 as the fulfillment of the words in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The burning of the skull was the 'another' punishment promised for יהויקים.

steps.title: The Hasmonean court's decree, as reported by רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that the בית דין של חשמונאי decreed that one who has relations with a גויה is liable on four counts: נדה, שפחה, גויה, and אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: The court of the חשמונאים decreed that one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman is liable for her on account of נדה, שפחה, גויה, and אשת איש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier topic of הבא על הגויה. רב דימי reports a rabbinic decree that treats such a man as liable on four separate counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law these counts do not fully apply to a non-Jewish woman. The חשמונאים added them as a decree to keep people far from this sin. רב דימי's list includes אשת איש, which treats her as if she were a married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbinic court in the days of the Hasmonean kings
They made a decree, a rabbinic law
A woman in her menstrual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: This is a rabbinic decree, not a Torah-level punishment. The four counts are added by the חשמונאים to keep people away from this sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that besides the punishment from heaven in step 5, the חכמים added their own penalties for this sin.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
The court of the Hasmoneans decreed:
one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman
is liable for her on account of
a niddah, a maidservant, a non-Jewish woman, and a married woman.
phrases.notes: The first letters of these four spell נשג״א, a memory aid that sets up the next line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about יהויקים and returns to the הלכה of הבא על הגויה from steps 4 and 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By decree of the חשמונאים, one who has relations with a גויה is liable on account of נדה, שפחה, גויה, and אשת איש.

steps.title: רבין's version: a זונה, not a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רבין agrees with three of the counts but replaces אשת איש with זונה. He holds that non-Jews do not have real marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: On account of נשג״ז, which is נדה, שפחה, גויה, and זונה. But on account of marriage, they do not have it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין gives a different report of the same decree. He swaps out אשת איש for זונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on נדה, שפחה, and גויה. The argument is only about the fourth item. רבין says non-Jews have no binding marriage, so the woman cannot be counted as an אשת איש. Instead, she is treated like a זונה.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
On account of נשג״ז:
phrases.notes: Same memory aid as before, but the last letter is ז, for זונה, instead of א, for אשת איש.

phrases.english: a niddah, a maidservant, a non-Jewish woman, and a zonah.
But on account of marriage, they do not have it.
phrases.notes: Non-Jews don't have marriage in the halachic sense, so the married-woman count can't apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second report of the same decree. It argues with רב דימי only on the fourth item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decree makes him liable for נדה, שפחה, גויה, and זונה, but not for אשת איש, since non-Jews have no halachic marriage.

steps.title: Why רב דימי still counts a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב דימי's view: non-Jews certainly do not abandon their wives, so a non-Jew's wife counts as a married woman for this decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רב דימי, holds: they certainly do not abandon their wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב דימי's answer to רבין's reasoning. It explains why he kept אשת איש on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין said non-Jews have no marriage. רב דימי replies that in practice, non-Jews stay committed to their wives. So for this decree, the חכמים treated such a woman like a married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one; how does the other opinion answer?

steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי and רבין agree the חשמונאים decreed liability for נדה, שפחה, and גויה. They argue about the fourth item: רב דימי counts אשת איש because non-Jews stay with their wives, while רבין counts זונה because non-Jews have no halachic marriage.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: The other one is רב דימי. How would he answer רבין?

phrases.english: Their wives they certainly do not abandon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב דימי's list from step 11 against רבין's reasoning in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning of the other opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since non-Jews lack halachic marriage, the married-woman count should not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: In practice, non-Jews are committed to their wives, so the decree treats a non-Jew's wife as a married woman.

steps.title: רב חסדא: We do not instruct one who asks
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that if a person asks בית דין whether he may kill a man who is with a גויה, the court does not tell him that he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: If someone comes to ask, we do not tell him to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a limit to the rule that zealots may strike a man who has relations with a גויה. If the zealot stops to ask בית דין first, they will not give him permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right of קנאים is not a normal court ruling. It works only when a person acts on his own, in the heat of the moment. Once someone asks, בית דין will not give him a היתר to kill.

keyTerms.meaning: One who comes to ask for advice or permission
We do not instruct him (we do not give a ruling allowing it)
Zealots may strike him (the background rule being limited here)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the act is forbidden to a zealot. It means only that בית דין will not give permission ahead of time when asked.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the zealot's right is a very unusual exception and not a regular court process.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
One who comes to consult, we do not instruct him [to kill].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the בית דין של חשמונאי decree back to the rule of קנאים and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who asks whether he may act as a קנאי is not told that he may.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A second report, from רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן, states the very same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone comes to ask, we do not tell him to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב חסדא. רבי יוחנן said exactly the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase איתמר נמי means a second, separate teaching agrees with the first. This makes רב חסדא's rule stronger, since a major אמורא in ארץ ישראל taught it too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a second teaching that matches)

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who comes to consult, we do not instruct him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14 with the same ruling from another chain of teachers.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that one who asks is not told to act
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: The zealot may act only during the act
steps.stepSummary: If זמרי had separated from the woman and פנחס then killed him, פנחס would be executed. If זמרי had turned and killed פנחס, זמרי would not be executed, because פנחס counts as a רודף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover, if זמרי had separated and פנחס killed him, פנחס would be executed for it. If זמרי had turned and killed פנחס, he would not be executed for it, since פנחס was a pursuer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן's statement continues with "ולא עוד אלא" and adds two more limits to the zealot's right, using זמרי and פנחס as the example. The killing is allowed only during the act, and the sinner may even defend himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the act stops, killing the sinner is plain murder, and the zealot is liable. While the zealot is attacking, the sinner is not under a court death sentence, so he may treat the zealot as a רודף and kill him in self-defense.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that, but even more
A pursuer trying to kill someone; it is allowed to kill him to save the victim

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds strange that the sinner may kill the righteous zealot. The point is that the zealot's right is allowed but never required or backed by בית דין, so the sinner keeps his right of self-defense.
steps.whyThisMatters: Steps 14 to 16 together show how narrow and risky the קנאים rule is.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם פֵּירַשׁ זִמְרִי
phrases.english: And not only that, but if Zimri had separated
and Pinchas killed him, he would be executed for him.
If Zimri had turned around and killed Pinchas,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נֶהֱרָג עָלָיו, שֶׁהֲרֵי רוֹדֵף הוּא.
phrases.english: he would not be executed for him, since he [Pinchas] is a pursuer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם פֵּירַשׁ זִמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's statement from step 15 ("ולא עוד אלא"), adding more limits to the קנאים rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קנאי may kill only during the act. Afterward it is murder, and the sinner may kill the zealot as a רודף.

steps.title: שבט שמעון pushes זמרי to act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the story behind the פסוק. After משה tells the judges to execute the sinners, שבט שמעון complains to their leader זמרי that he is silent while they are being judged for death.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And משה said to the judges of Israel...' The tribe of שמעון went to זמרי בן סלוא and said to him: They are judging capital cases, and you sit and stay quiet?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling the story of זמרי, based on the פסוק in במדבר. This step sets up the background for what זמרי does next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judges were executing people who sinned with בעל פעור, and many of them were from שבט שמעון. The tribe pressures its נשיא to defend them.

keyTerms.meaning: Capital cases (cases where a person can be sentenced to death)
זמרי son of סלוא, the נשיא of שבט שמעון

phrases.english: "And Moses said to the judges of Israel, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:5

phrases.english: The tribe of Shimon went

phrases.aramaic: אֵצֶל זִמְרִי בֶּן סָלוּא, אָמְרוּ לוֹ:
phrases.english: to Zimri son of Salu, and said to him:
They are judging capital cases,
and you are sitting and staying silent?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having used זמרי and פנחס as an example, the גמרא now tells their full story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבט שמעון pressured זמרי to respond to the executions.

steps.title: זמרי approaches כזבי
steps.stepSummary: זמרי gathers 24,000 people and goes to כזבי. She says she may submit only to the greatest leader. זמרי answers that he is greater than משה, because שמעון was יעקב's second son and לוי the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he do? He got up, gathered 24,000 from Israel, and went to כזבי. He said to her: Submit to me. She said: I am a king's daughter, and my father commanded me to submit only to the greatest of them. He said: He too is a tribal leader. Not only that, he is greater than him, since he is the second from the womb and that one is the third.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. זמרי tries to convince כזבי by claiming a higher rank than משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כזבי wants the greatest leader, meaning משה. זמרי twists ייחוס to argue that he comes from an older tribe, so he outranks משה. He speaks about himself in the third person as 'he'.

keyTerms.meaning: Second from the womb (the second-born son)

phrases.english: What did he do? He stood up and gathered
twenty-four thousand from Israel
and went to Cozbi.
He said to her: Submit to me.
She said to him: I am a king's daughter,
and this is what my father commanded me:
Submit only to the greatest of them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: אַף הוּא נְשִׂיא שֵׁבֶט הוּא,
phrases.english: He said to her: He too is the head of a tribe,
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is זמרי talking about himself.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ,
phrases.english: and not only that, he is greater than him,
phrases.notes: 'Than him' means משה.

phrases.english: since he is second from the womb
and that one is third from the womb.
phrases.notes: שמעון was יעקב's second son, and לוי, משה's ancestor, was the third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows זמרי's response to the tribe's pressure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זמרי claims to be greater than משה in order to win over כזבי.

steps.title: זמרי challenges משה in public
steps.stepSummary: זמרי grabs כזבי by her hair, brings her to משה, and asks whether she is forbidden or permitted. He adds that if she is forbidden, then who permitted the daughter of יתרו to משה?
steps.simpleTranslation: He grabbed her by her forelock and brought her to משה. He said to him: Son of עמרם, is this one forbidden or permitted? And if you say forbidden, who permitted the daughter of יתרו to you?
steps.whatsHappening: זמרי turns the story into a public challenge against משה. He uses משה's own marriage to argue that a Midianite woman must be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's wife צפורה was a Midianite, the daughter of יתרו. זמרי argues that if a Midianite woman is forbidden, משה's own marriage would be wrong. He calls him 'בן עמרם' rather than 'משה רבינו' to show disrespect.

keyTerms.meaning: Forelock (a lock of hair at the front of the head)
Son of עמרם (a disrespectful way to address משה)
The daughter of יתרו, צפורה, משה's wife

steps.confusionAlert: זמרי's argument is not a real question in learning. In the story, it works as a public attack on משה.

phrases.english: He seized her by her forelock
and brought her to Moses.
He said to him: Son of Amram,
is this one forbidden or permitted?
And if you say forbidden,
who permitted the daughter of Yitro to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After winning over כזבי, זמרי brings the conflict right in front of משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זמרי publicly challenges משה, using משה's marriage to the daughter of יתרו.

steps.title: משה forgets the הלכה and פנחס steps forward
steps.stepSummary: משה forgets the הלכה about what to do in this case. Everyone bursts into tears, which explains the פסוק 'and they were weeping at the entrance of the אהל מועד.' Then the next פסוק says that פנחס saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה slipped away from him. They all broke out crying, and that is what is written: 'And they were weeping at the entrance of the אהל מועד.' And it is written: 'And פנחס son of אלעזר saw.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its turning point, and the גמרא links it to the פסוקים. The quote 'וירא פנחס' sets up the next part, where the גמרא will explain what פנחס saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה that slipped away is the rule of קנאים פוגעין בו, which allows a zealot to strike someone in the middle of this sin. Since משה and the judges could not act, the way was open for פנחס, who remembered the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה was hidden from him (he forgot it)
And that is what is written (linking the story to a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of קנאים is very narrow. No ruling is given to one who asks, it applies only during the act, and the sinner may defend himself. The story of זמרי shows the one famous moment when this rule was used, after משה himself forgot the הלכה.

phrases.english: The halacha eluded him.
They all burst out weeping,
and that is what is written:
"And they were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting."
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:6

phrases.english: And it is written: "And Pinchas son of Elazar saw."
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of זמרי's challenge and moves the story toward פנחס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה forgot the הלכה, everyone wept, and the פסוק turns to פנחס.

steps.title: What did פנחס see?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means when it says פנחס 'saw.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he see?
steps.whatsHappening: The פסוק said 'and פנחס saw,' and the גמרא asks what exactly he saw. This short question sets up three different answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone else was there too, yet only פנחס acted. The גמרא wants to know what פנחס saw or realized that pushed him to act when nobody else did.

phrases.english: What did he see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the words 'ויַרְא פינחס' quoted in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did פנחס see or realize that made him act?

steps.title: רב: He remembered the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב says פנחס saw the sin and remembered the הלכה that zealots may strike someone who is with a non-Jewish woman. משה answers that the one who remembers it should carry it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: He saw the act and remembered the הלכה. He said to משה: 'Brother of my father's father, didn't you teach me when you came down from הר סיני: one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman, zealots may strike him?' משה said to him: 'Let the one who reads the letter be the messenger who carries it out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: watching the sin reminded פנחס of the הלכה that משה had forgotten. משה tells him that since he remembered it, he should be the one to act on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties straight back to step 20, where משה forgot the הלכה. פנחס remembered it, and משה gave him the job of carrying it out.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has relations with a non-Jewish woman
The one who reads the letter
Messenger or agent who carries out an order

phrases.english: Rav says:
He saw the act and remembered the halakha.
He said to him: Brother of my father's father,
phrases.notes: He's talking to משה, who was the brother of אהרן, פנחס's grandfather.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כָּךְ לִימַּדְתַּנִי בְּרִדְתְּךָ מֵהַר סִינַי:
phrases.english: didn't you teach me this when you came down from Mount Sinai:
one who has relations with a non-Jewish woman, zealots strike him?
He said to him: The one who reads the letter
let him be the messenger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב רָאָה מַעֲשֶׂה וְנִזְכַּר הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He saw the sin and remembered the הלכה of קנאין פוגעין בו, which משה had forgotten.

steps.title: שמואל: When God's name is shamed, don't wait for the teacher
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says פנחס understood the פסוק 'there is no wisdom against ה׳': when there is חילול השם, you do not stop to honor your teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: He saw that 'there is no wisdom, no understanding, and no counsel against ה׳.' Anywhere there is חילול השם, we do not give honor to the teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer. פנחס realized that, because God's name was being shamed, he could act right away without first asking משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a student does not rule on הלכה in front of his teacher. שמואל explains why פנחס could act on his own here: חילול השם pushes aside the usual respect for the teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not give honor to the teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lasting rule: when God's name is being shamed, you act right away and do not wait out of respect for your teacher.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
He saw that there is no wisdom and no understanding
and no counsel against the Lord.
phrases.notes: משלי 21:30

phrases.english: Anywhere that there is desecration of God's name,
we do not give honor to the teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 21, different from רב's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He understood that חילול השם overrides honoring the teacher, so he acted without asking משה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: He saw an angel destroying the people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says in the name of רבי אליעזר that פנחס saw an angel striking the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי אליעזר: He saw that an angel came and was destroying among the people.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer. פנחס saw an angel bringing destruction on the nation, so he knew he had to act right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason is the danger to the people, not a remembered הלכה or a rule about honoring the teacher. The plague had already started, so stopping the sin would save lives.

keyTerms.meaning: And was destroying among the people

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to 'what did פנחס see': רב says he remembered the הלכה; שמואל says חילול השם overrides honoring the teacher; רבי אליעזר says he saw an angel destroying the people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
He saw that an angel came and was destroying among the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר רָאָה שֶׁבָּא מַלְאָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He saw an angel destroying the people and knew he had to act at once.

steps.title: No weapons in the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'he rose from the congregation and took a spear,' the גמרא learns that one may not enter the בית המדרש with weapons.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.' From here we learn that one may not enter the בית המדרש with weapons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next פסוק in the story. It learns a הלכה from the order of the words: first he left, and only then he took the spear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'congregation' was the gathering of the judges and the Torah study. Since פנחס took the spear only after leaving that gathering, we learn that weapons do not belong inside the בית המדרש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical הלכה about respecting the בית המדרש: weapons are not brought inside.

phrases.english: "He rose from among the congregation
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:7

phrases.english: and took a spear in his hand."
From here we learn that one does not enter
the study hall with weapons.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיכָּן שֶׁאֵין נִכְנָסִין בִּכְלֵי זַיִין לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story and reads the next פסוק after 'פנחס saw.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not enter the בית המדרש with weapons, learned from the order of the words in the פסוק.

steps.title: פנחס hides the spear's blade
steps.stepSummary: פנחס takes the blade off the spear and hides it in his clothing. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He removed its blade and put it in his garment, and he was...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts describing how פנחס carried the spear so no one would notice. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the blade made the spear look harmless, so he could walk toward זמרי without raising suspicion. The word 'and he was' leads into the next part of the description.

phrases.english: He removed its blade
and placed it in his garment,
and he was
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the spear in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פנחס hid the blade of the spear in his garment so the spear would not look like a weapon.
